header:
Date: 2026-08-26 | Start: 10:00 AM PDT | Duration: 42 min
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Redwood SE), Rina Sato (Redwood CSM), Samir Gupta (NexaHealth Head of ML), Lena Ortiz (Eng Mgr), Priya Menon (Security), Tom Baker (Infra), Anya Reddy (Data Scientist)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — can you hear me?
[00:06] Samir: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:09] Lena: Here.
[00:12] Jordan: Jordan on the call — se, from Redwood.
[00:16] Priya: Priya here from security.
[00:19] Maya: Great. Agenda — onboarding progress, access setup status, results from last week's small-scale run, and next steps for environment readiness.
[00:34] Tom: I can kick off infra — we finished the VPC peering test but had a couple of route table issues, so one of the subnets couldn't reach the Redwood demo endpoint, but we resolved it yesterday.
[00:46] Carlos: Cool thanks. To recap results quickly: we ran the 1k-token pipeline with 10 concurrent clients on rtx-a100-like instance and saw median latency ~220ms per token in the gen path, tail at 1.2s, cost estimates look in line with earlier numbers. There was some jitter around kv cache misses.
[01:09] Anya: Quick question — the cache misses, are those due to different request prefixes or session affinity?
[01:16] Jordan: Mostly session affinity — we had not enabled sticky routing in that run so some sessions were routed to different pods, losing KV cache. Enabling session pinning drops tail latency significantly.
[01:29] Priya: From security POV we need to confirm encryption at rest — is the model disk encrypted and do you integrate with our KMS?
[01:36] Maya: Yes — for Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM integration. For Dedicated we can configure key access with the key ARN. We still need the KMS policy from Tom to finish the setup.
[01:50] Tom: I'll share the key ARN after today's call — we just need to confirm key rotation policy, but should be fine.
[01:57] Lena: Onboarding checklist — we still can't access the console from our SSO. I opened a ticket with SAML metadata, but the test assertion keeps failing.
[02:06] Rina: We saw that — Maya, Carlos, can you help with the SAML config?
[02:12] Carlos: Sure. Common issue is clock skew or audience URI mismatch. I'll re-check the metadata and share a quick how-to.
[02:20] Samir: Also, about model selection: we test both redwood-rlhf-v2 and an open LLM, we saw better qualitative results on some of our prompts with redwood-rlhf-v2 but cost was higher. Any recommendations on tuning to reduce cost?
[02:36] Jordan: There are a few levers — quantization to int8/4 where compatible, prompt engineering to reduce context window, and prefix caching for repeated prompts. For your batch workload, dynamic batching plus KV cache can cut token cost by up to 30% in our experience.
[02:52] Anya: We did a quick run with 8-bit and saw small accuracy drift on numeric extraction tasks. Is there a recommended fall-back?
[03:01] Carlos: If numeric fidelity is critical, keep FP16 on the output layers or use mixed precision — quantize embeddings and mid layers but keep logits numeric stable. We'll provide a config recommendation.
[03:12] Priya: Back to compliance — do you log access to model artifacts and inference requests? We need audit logs showing data access for our compliance team.
[03:21] Maya: Yes, we emit audit logs for inference requests, model loads, and key accesses. They can be forwarded to your SIEM or stored in an S3 bucket with retention controls. We'll share the schema of logs.
[03:35] Lena: Good. For the runtime sizing call — what's the next step to get production-like throughput numbers?
[03:42] Jordan: We need representative traffic patterns and sample prompts. Anya, if you can drop the golden prompts and per-request token distributions into the shared drive we'll rerun with canary traffic and give sizing guidance.
[03:53] Anya: I'll upload by EOD tomorrow.
[03:56] [04:00] Maya: Quick note on the bench spreadsheet — we updated it with 95th pct, p50, token counts and cost per 1k tokens. I'll send the link after the call.
[04:08] Tom: Thanks — I need the 95th percentile numbers to plan autoscale and burst.
[04:14] Carlos: On environment readiness: we found one gap — outbound egress to Redwood endpoints requires an allowlist on the proxy. For private deploys we'll need full private link config.
[04:27] Samir: For the pilot we planned private deploy but maybe start on dedicated first? What are tradeoffs?
[04:33] Maya: Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and easier onboarding; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you stronger network isolation and control for regulated data. Many customers start on Dedicated and then migrate to Private once SSO/KMS/audit requirements are locked down.
[04:49] Priya: We're leaning Private due to PHI concerns, but we'd like to avoid long delays. What is typical timeline?
[04:55] Rina: For Private, typical lead is 6-8 weeks after contract — includes network alignment, KMS, and on-prem packaging if required. Dedicated can be standing up in 1-2 weeks.
[05:08] Lena: Ok, that helps. On integration we still need service account creds for your API tests — last creds expired.
[05:15] Maya: I'll re-issue temporary tokens and upload to the shared vault. Carlos will coordinate.
[05:20] Carlos: I'll rotate the test service account and add IP restrictions as requested.
[05:25] [06:00] Jordan: I want to call out an anomaly from the last run — when we simulated a long context (3k tokens) the memory usage spiked and one pod OOMed. We suspect KV cache pressure with parallel sessions. Need to tune eviction policy and maybe increase per-pod memory.
[06:40] Tom: Did you get pod logs? We can send them but need to strip out PII.
[06:46] Jordan: Yes we have logs and traces; Maya will share a sanitized bundle.
[06:50] Maya: Yep, will upload to the secure link.
[06:54] Anya: On evaluation metrics — we want to track hallucination rate on extraction tasks. Can Redwood integrate with our eval harness?
[07:02] Carlos: Yes, we can plug into your eval scripts and report per-run quality drift. We can set up daily evals against golden set and trigger alerts on regression.
[07:13] Priya: For auditability please make sure eval outputs are stored with request IDs so we can trace back.
[07:19] Carlos: Absolutely.
[07:22] [08:00] Samir: About SSO again — I forwarded the SAML metadata to Rina. Any idea why the assertion fails?
[08:07] Rina: It was the audience URI and a missing nameID format. I asked them to switch from email to persistent.
[08:14] Lena: We'll try that.
[08:16] Tom: One more infra ask — can Redwood support VPC peering + private link together? We need DNS resolution for the service endpoint.
[08:24] Jordan: We support both — private link is recommended for Private deployments; Dedicated can use peering with proper route tables. We'll work with your network team for DNS setup.
[08:34] [09:00] Maya: Quick recap of next actions — share bench sheet, upload logs, rotate creds, collect prompts, and Tom to provide KMS ARN. Anything missing?
[09:45] Priya: SOC2 cert and questionnaire from our side — Priya will send but we also need Redwood's data flow diagram.
[09:52] Maya: I'll include our data flow and SOC2 scope doc in the packet.
[09:57] Anya: For the tuning story — can you provide a sample quantization profile and the expected accuracy delta for our numeric extractor?
[10:05] Carlos: Yes — will include quant profiles and a recommendation to keep last-layer FP16 for numeric tasks.
[10:12] Samir: Regarding cost, if we enable prefix caching and session pinning what's realistic cost reduction?
[10:18] Jordan: We're seeing 20-35% token cost reduction depending on reuse. For query-heavy workloads with repeated prompts you hit the higher end.
[10:26] Lena: OK. Timeline wise we want a decision on Dedicated vs Private by next Friday 2026-09-03.
[10:34] Maya: Noted. We'll have sizing and cost estimates to help.
[10:37] [11:00] Maya: any final questions?
[11:02] Tom: No, I'll follow up with KMS and routing info.
[11:05] Priya: I'll send SOC2 items.
[11:07] Maya: Thanks all, we'll send the follow-ups and the benchmark link.
[11:12] [End 10:42]
